title: Erdafitinib: targeted tablets
indication_text: Unresectable/metastatic urothelial carcinoma with susceptible FGFR3 alteration after at least one PD1/PDL1-containing line in that setting.
purpose: Help control advanced urothelial cancer with a susceptible FGFR3 alteration after previous PD1/PDL1 treatment.
schedule_label: Daily tablets · early phosphate review on days 14–21
schedule_summary: The usual starting dose is8 mg once daily. The team may increase it to9 mg after reviewing phosphate and toxicity on days 14–21. Never change the dose yourself. Treatment is continuous until progression or unacceptable toxicity; the28-day view is only a reference.
administration_text: Swallow tablets whole, with or without food, at about the same time each day. Avoid grapefruit and Seville oranges. If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible and resume the usual schedule next day; never take extra tablets. If you vomit after a dose, take the next dose the following day.
monitoring_summary: Phosphate is checked on days 14–21 and monthly afterwards, more often if elevated. Eye examinations are monthly for the first four months and every three months thereafter; new symptoms need prompt review. Repeat blood count, kidney/liver tests, electrolytes and ECG under the prescribed plan.
safety_note: Follow your own prescription and hospital instructions. This information supports a discussion; it does not authorise treatment.
urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999.

agents.name: Erdafitinib
agents.explanation: Some urothelial cancers use an altered fibroblast growth factor receptor, FGFR3, to drive growth. Erdafitinib blocks this signal. FGFR also helps regulate phosphate handling, explaining why blood phosphate may rise.
risks: High phosphate and other electrolyte changes; prolonged elevation may harm tissues
Retinal fluid/central serous retinopathy, blurred vision and other eye problems
Sore mouth, dry mouth, altered taste and reduced appetite
Nail changes/infection, dry skin, rash and painful palms or soles
Diarrhoea, fatigue, hair changes and liver/kidney-test changes
agents.watch: Report any new blurred vision, visual distortion or eye pain promptly; do not wait for the next routine eye appointment.

anatomy: New blurred or distorted vision or eye pain needs prompt eye assessment.
Report soreness, dry mouth or difficulty eating and drinking.
Report painful nails, infected nail folds, rash or sore palms/soles.
Report frequent diarrhoea, pain or dehydration.
Blood tests detect high phosphate, often before symptoms. Follow the agreed diet and binder plan.
Blood tests check the liver. Report yellow eyes or dark urine.
Tell the team about worsening tiredness, dizziness or sudden illness.
Report palpitations or faintness and show the team all medicines and supplements.

rows.label: Medicines and practical care
cells: Confirm the tablet strength, daily dose, early phosphate appointment and baseline eye examination before starting.

Swallow tablets whole, with or without food, at about the same time each day. Avoid grapefruit and Seville oranges. If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible and resume the usual schedule next day; never take extra tablets. If you vomit after a dose, take the next dose the following day.

High phosphate may need a dietitian-guided phosphate restriction and prescribed phosphate binder. Do not add vitaminD supplements without oncology review. Ask about mouth care, skin/nail care, diarrhoea treatment and dry-eye support. Bring all medicines and supplements for interaction checking.

evidence.title: THOR randomised phase III study
evidence.summary: After previous PD1/PDL1 therapy, median overall survival was 12.1 months with erdafitinib versus 7.8 months with chemotherapy (hazard ratio0.64;95% confidence interval0.47–0.88). Median progression-free survival was 5.6 versus 2.7 months.
evidence.intro: After previous PD1/PDL1 therapy, median overall survival was 12.1 months with erdafitinib versus 7.8 months with chemotherapy (hazard ratio0.64;95% confidence interval0.47–0.88). Median progression-free survival was 5.6 versus 2.7 months.
evidence.caveat: These are trial group estimates, not a personal prognosis. Trial molecular eligibility included FGFR3/2 alterations; the current Irish indication requires susceptible FGFR3 alterations.
evidence.interpretation: These are trial group estimates, not a personal prognosis. Trial molecular eligibility included FGFR3/2 alterations; the current Irish indication requires susceptible FGFR3 alterations.

questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: Help control advanced urothelial cancer with a susceptible FGFR3 alteration after previous PD1/PDL1 treatment. FGFR testing selects people whose tumour may respond to this mechanism. Treatment aims to control cancer; scans and symptoms assess benefit separately from phosphate and other safety tests. Other systemic treatment or symptom-directed radiotherapy depends on your individual situation.

The usual starting dose is8 mg once daily. The team may increase it to9 mg after reviewing phosphate and toxicity on days 14–21. Never change the dose yourself. Treatment is continuous until progression or unacceptable toxicity; the28-day view is only a reference.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.
